what: Southwest Airlines is a major US domestic airline. It flies only Boeing 737s, serves mostly point-to-point routes rather than hubs, and for decades let passengers check bags free and choose seats on boarding, both of which it has now changed.
customers: American leisure and business travellers flying domestically and to nearby international destinations.
money: ticket revenue, now including bag and seat fees
loyalty programme payments from card partners and cargo
moat: A single aircraft type that simplifies maintenance and crew scheduling, plus a brand built on customer goodwill, though both advantages have narrowed.
risks: Operating margin of about 2% is far below its historical level and below major rivals
A December 2022 operational meltdown damaged its reputation and brought regulatory penalties
Charging for bags and assigning seats removes the differences customers chose it for
Boeing delivery delays have limited fleet growth
opportunities: New revenue from bag fees, assigned seating and premium rows adds billions annually
An activist investor has pushed through cost and revenue changes
Debt of about $7 billion against $3.6 billion of cash is modest for an airline
watch: Revenue per available seat mile and the margin gap against Delta and United.
